zh: 利润按天独立相加。答案=原利润+修改带来的最大增益，而“不修改”对应增益0，所以负的原利润不能被当成0，也不能强制修改。
修改窗口[l,l+k)后：前半段贡献变为0，后半段贡献变为对应价格之和，窗口外不变。因此增益=后半段价格和−窗口原贡献和，两者都能在窗口右移时O(1)更新。
先算每天的贡献rates[i]×strategy[i]和原利润；初始化第一个窗口的原贡献和old与后半段价格和rep，best=max(0,rep−old)；窗口每右移一步，old加入新右端、去掉左端，rep加入rates[l+k]、去掉rates[l+k/2]，再更新best；输出原利润+best，用64位整数。
en: Profit adds up day by day. The answer is the original profit plus the largest gain from a modification, and not modifying is a gain of 0, so a negative original profit must not be turned into 0, and the modification is not forced.

After modifying window [l, l+k), the first half contributes 0, the second half contributes the sum of its prices, and everything outside is unchanged. So the gain is (second-half price sum) - (original contribution of the window), and both sums update in O(1) as the window slides right.

Compute each day's contribution rates[i] * strategy[i] and the original profit; initialize the first window's original contribution old and second-half price sum rep, best = max(0, rep - old); on each slide add the new right end to old and drop the left end, add rates[l+k] to rep and drop rates[l+k/2], then update best; print original profit + best with 64-bit integers.

explanationEn:
## Fixed source, optional modification, and the companion page of the same problem

OA LIST/SIG_OA/001_image.txt at the pinned commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc states clearly: in strategy, -1 means buy, 0 means do nothing, and 1 means sell; the profit is the sum of all selling prices minus the sum of all buying prices and may be negative. The original NOTE guarantees that there is always enough currency and funds, so inventory and budget are not simulated, and buying before selling is not required.

001 uses "may change": the strategy may be left unmodified; if it is modified, choose a contiguous window of length exactly k, set its first k/2 items to 0 and its last k/2 items to 1, and leave the other positions unchanged. This is an optional single modification and must not be misread as a forced modification or as repeated modifications. To make the practical difference of optionality explicit, this site adds rates=[1,1], strategy=[1,1], k=2: without modification the profit is 2, while a forced modification gives only 1. The original phrase "choose the range optimally" means that when the modification is used, the best window is chosen; it does not cancel the meaning of "may".

SIG003 itself gives the complete range of n as 2..100000, rates[i] in 1..1000, and strategy of the same length with values -1/0/1; only k is truncated at the title. The range of k is completed from the pinned identical problem eBay_OA/023_image.txt: even and 2<=k<=nums.length. Its nums is a variable-name slip on that page; the only array length in this task is the common length n of rates/strategy, so this problem publicly normalizes it to 2<=k<=n. The correspondence does not rest on the title alone: eBay019/020 and SIG001/002 agree on the rules, the no-budget NOTE, the complete example arrays/strategy/k=4, and the answer 18. Only the missing k range is supplemented; the price upper bound from another company's page does not replace SIG's own explicit bound of 1000.

The original example rates=[2,4,1,5,10,6], strategy=[-1,1,0,1,-1,0], k=4 has original profit -3, the three modification windows give -4, 13, and 18, and the answer 18 is kept. The other two public examples are added by this site. The input is n k, the price array, and the strategy array; the output is one integer; upstream code was not executed.

## Approach

Denote the original profit by B. When window [l,l+k) is modified, remove the window's original contribution old and add the second-half price sum replacement; the net gain is replacement-old. Not modifying corresponds to gain 0. Enumerate all windows; the maximum profit is B plus the maximum of 0 and all gains.

The reference implementation maintains the window's original contribution sum and its second-half price sum. When the window moves right by 1, the original contribution drops the left end and adds the new right end; the second half drops the old l+k/2 and adds the new l+k; both sums are updated in O(1). When k=n there is only the first window, and the loop is naturally empty.

## Proof of correctness

Profit adds up independently day by day, and the original NOTE rules out any extra effect of funds or inventory on whether operations are feasible. Items outside the modification window are unchanged; the first half of the window is set to 0 and contributes 0, and the second half is set to 1 and contributes the corresponding prices, so removing old and adding replacement gives exactly the true profit after modifying that window.

The initialization covers the first window exactly. Each slide removes only the element that leaves and adds only the element that enters, so the two maintained sums always equal the current window's original contribution and its second-half price sum. The starting points 0..n-k cover exactly all valid windows, with none missed. A valid strategy either keeps the original or modifies one of these windows, so taking the maximum of gain 0 and all window gains gives the optimal profit.

## Complexity and numeric bounds

Computing the original contributions and scanning the windows take O(n) time in total; storing the input and contributions takes O(n) space, and the sliding window uses O(1) extra. Every item of the final strategy is still -1/0/1, so the absolute profit is <=1000n<=10^8; Python integers or 64-bit integers suffice for intermediate values. A negative optimal profit must not be clamped to 0: not modifying yields the original profit, not zero profit.

## Independent verification

The small-domain oracle copies the strategy array, actually writes 0 into the first half and 1 into the second half for each window, and then computes the profit day by day from the start, also comparing with the unmodified plan; it uses no gain or sliding recurrence. 163 unique oracle cases passed through real subprocesses, and an exhaustive search over n=2..5, prices 1/2, strategies -1/0/1, and all valid even k covered 18396 cases.

For the large domain, two separate prefix arrays of prices and original contributions are built, and each window's interval difference is computed independently, without the reference's adjacent-window recurrence. Full n=100000 covers all-buy/all-sell/all-hold, price endpoints, k=2 and k=n, the largest even k for the largest odd n, optima at the start and at the end, extremely unbalanced window halves, and fixed random data. Some large cases are also confirmed by closed forms. The negative controls respectively force a modification and misplace the selling half into the first half; a kill is counted only after all official inputs exit normally.
